Project assistant, part-time (40%).

CHF 1,430 gross per month, paid twelve times a year.

Emmen, 26 April 2022

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Was the employment relationship agreed for a fixed term, with an agreed end date, rather than for an unlimited period?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the employer give as the cause of the dismissal the employee's absence from work, and does the employee say they were prevented from working through no fault of their own (for instance illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the immediate dismissal in writing?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employer end the employment relationship with immediate effect, without a notice period?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Has the employee earned income from other work during the time the notice period or the agreed term would still have run?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam

Please find attached my employment contract with Weidgrund Holdings Ltd in Emmen.

On 19 January 2026 Hannah Schneider, the head of administration, called me in and told me I was dismissed with immediate effect. I had to pack my things and leave the same afternoon. There was no notice period and no warning beforehand.

Two days later, on 21 January, I wrote to Ms Schneider by e-mail and asked her to give me the reasons for this dismissal in writing. I want to see on paper why they think they could do this.

The contract I had was a fixed one. I started on 5 May 2022 and it was agreed to run until 4 May 2026, because I was hired for a four-year project. That end date is in the contract.

Whether I've earned anything since is honestly hard to say. At the end of January I did a translation for a former client, Mark Huber, and sent him an invoice for CHF 945. He now says the translation wasn't what he ordered and he won't pay it, at least not in full. We are still arguing about it, so I might get the money or I might get nothing.

I've also attached my last pay slip, which shows my salary of CHF 1,430 a month for my part-time post.

I would like to know what I can claim for the months up to May.

Yours faithfully
Nina Tanner
Kirchgasse 36, Emmen
